Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear examples. Short answers up front, then a worked example:

Policy summary (current Redwood hosted API billing):
- System messages are tokenized and counted as input tokens each time they are sent to the model, unless you use the "service-side" system override that pins the system prompt server-side for the session (not available by default). In your case, because the system content is included in each request, it is billed as input.
- Tool-return content: when a tool is invoked and the tool returns text that the model incorporates into its final output, the tool-return tokens are billed as OUTPUT tokens. If a tool return is resubmitted as input for a subsequent model call, those tokens would also be billed again as input on that subsequent call.
- Rounding: Redwood token accounting does per-request tokenization with integer token counts (no fractional tokens). We round up token math per request (i.e., each request's pre- and post-token counts are integerized, then aggregated on the invoice). There is no extra per-tool rounding beyond that.

Worked example from your sample (approx):
- single request: client sends prompt (user) = 420 tokens; system prompt = 28 tokens; -> input subtotal = 448 tokens (rounded up to 448).
- model produces draft that invokes 'search' tool; tool returns 170 tokens (tool-return). The model then emits final response that includes 95 tokens of generated text (post-tool).
- billing attribution: input = 448 tokens; output = 170 (tool return, billed as output) + 95 (model generated output) = 265 tokens. Total billed tokens for that request = 713.

Note: if your integration sequences the tool-return through a separate subsequent model call (e.g., you capture the tool text then send a follow-up call that includes it as input), those tool tokens would be billed again as input on that subsequent call.

If the above matches your logs we can re-run counts and surface potential credits if we find an ingestion pattern we can optimize (for example: pinning system prompts server-side, or sending the tool content as attachments so the model doesn't re-tokenize them).

I'll ask Marissa to attach the reconciled CSV and a short delta calculation.

Hi Samantha — I ran your sample through our billing recount and here are the outcomes and clarifications. I included a small reconciled CSV at the Drive link; summary below.

Findings:
- Duplicate system prompt injections: we did observe 32 requests where your client-side hybrid streaming pattern sent the system prompt twice (partial + finalize). Both occurrences are tokenized and billed independently because the runtime receives them as separate input payloads. We flagged those 32 requests for a one-time goodwill credit (covering the duplicated system prompt tokens) as a gesture while you patch the client behavior.

- raw_tool_output behavior: by default, any text returned by a Redwood-hosted tool that the model ingests or that passes back to the API surface is counted as OUTPUT on that single request. If you set the integration to record raw_tool_output separately but do not re-submit it as a new input, it will not be double-billed as input; it remains output for that request. However, if you programmatically take raw_tool_output and then send it back in a subsequent request as part of the prompt, it will be billed again as input on that new request.

- Rounding and aggregation: our system tokenizes per request (we use an internal tokenization compatible with GPT-style tokenizers). We round to whole tokens at the request level, then aggregate. That means small fractional differences that appear when you re-tokenize with a different tokenizer can cause deltas. We reconciled using Redwood's tokenizer for the invoice.

Actions taken:
- We applied a one-time credit equal to the duplicated-system-token total for April (credit appears on next invoice).
- We shared the reconciled CSV to the Drive link you provided (see HubSpot note for access).
- Recommendations: consider server-side pinning of stable system prompts or switch to a session-scoped system prompt if you rely on streaming + finalize flows.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical sync with our SDK/Runtime engineer to walk through logs and best practices for minimizing token footprint.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
